newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dlr closes firmer, seen testing higher.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dlr closes firmer, seen testing higher.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed firmer and reasonably well bid on Wednesday despite a call from Reserve Bank governor Don Brash for a lower exchange rate and higher interest rates.
Brash told Reuters Financial Television in London that he would like a new mix of lower foreign exchange rates and higher interest rates to take the economy forward.
"He just repeated something he's probably said about five times already," said a chief bank dealer.
"I think higher interest rates and lower exchange rate doesn't really work, especially when the government's running a surplus and you've got sound economic fundamentals," he added.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.6979/86 and at 68.43 on its Trade-Weighted Index, up from 0.6962/69 and 68.18 at the open.
It traded a 0.6967-87 range during the session on light but steady volumes.
"It's been a very quiet day -- a little bit of domestic buying first thing, a little bit of offshore buying this afternoon, nothing large," the chief dealer said.
"Overall the currency looks quite well bid actually."
Dealers said there were rumours of renewed Japanese interest in the New Zealand currency, although no buying out of Tokyo had actually eventuated.
"There are rumours that Japanese interest may be coming back into the Kiwi; we haven't seen anything, but there just generally seems to be a bit of support for the unit at the moment," said one.
"It seems to have that bid undertone at the moment."
The Kiwi was seen testing higher overnight in a 0.6965-95 range.
